::: {.callout-warning}
## Draft
This is a proposed plan derived from the module topics. Exact dates, ordering,
and the split across sessions will be confirmed on ILIAS before the term starts.
:::

The course runs in three blocks: foundations, computation, and applications.
Each week pairs a 2-hour lecture with a 2-hour exercise session in which we
implement the week's method in Python.

## Block I — Foundations

| Week | Lecture | Exercise (Python) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Course intro; subjective probability and the Bayesian paradigm | Environment setup; NumPy/SciPy refresher |
| 2 | Bayes' theorem, priors, likelihoods, and the posterior | Conjugate Beta-Binomial and Normal models by hand |
| 3 | Point estimates, credible intervals, and prior sensitivity | Posterior summaries and prior-predictive checks |

: {.striped}

## Block II — Computation

| Week | Lecture | Exercise (Python) |
|---|---|---|
| 4 | Monte Carlo integration and the need for sampling | Importance sampling; Monte Carlo error |
| 5 | The Gibbs sampler | Gibbs sampler for the linear regression model |
| 6 | Metropolis-Hastings | Random-walk MH from scratch; tuning and diagnostics |
| 7 | Convergence diagnostics and efficient sampling | Trace plots, effective sample size, thinning |

: {.striped}

## Block III — Applications

| Week | Lecture | Exercise (Python) |
|---|---|---|
| 8 | Shrinkage and the Minnesota prior | Ridge-as-prior; shrinkage in high dimensions |
| 9 | Bayesian Vector Autoregressions (BVARs) | Estimating and forecasting a small BVAR |
| 10 | State-space models for macroeconomics | Kalman filter and time-varying parameters |
| 11 | Stochastic volatility and portfolio choice | SV model estimation; Bayesian portfolio weights |
| 12 | Bayesian machine learning for causal inference | BART-style models; treatment-effect estimation |
| 13 | Synthesis; exam preparation and review | Open lab; past-exam style problems |

: {.striped}

## Sessions and contact hours

The plan above spans roughly 13 teaching weeks, which matches the 60 contact
hours (2h lecture + 2h exercise per week) in the module description. The
remaining 120 hours are independent study: working through the exercises,
reading the literature, and preparing for the exam.
